title: Stale Estimate Step Added to the Allowance Rate
content:
# Service Training Note: The Stale Estimate Step on the Allowance Rate

## The rule the desk applies

Where the figure the bench priced on a work order of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service has stood for a long time, a step is added to the allowance rate carried on that order. The window it is measured against is the level's own estimate validity window.

1. Where the figure the bench priced has stood longer than twice the level's estimate validity window, the long stale-figure step of 10 percent is added to the allowance rate.
2. Where it has stood longer than that window but not twice it, the stale-figure step of 5 percent is added.
3. In any other case no step is added to the rate on this ground.

## Questions answered

**From when is the figure counted?** From the day the bench priced it, to the handling date.

**Which window applies?** The estimate validity window of the service level the work order runs at, in calendar days.

**What happens exactly at the window?** A figure that has stood exactly as long as the window has not stood longer than it, so clause 3 answers and no step is added. A figure that has stood exactly twice the window has not stood longer than twice it, so clause 2 answers and the step is 5 percent.

**Hypothetical readings.** At a level whose estimate validity window is 30 calendar days: a figure priced 20 days ago carries no step on this ground; one priced 31 days ago carries 5 percent; one priced 60 days ago carries 5 percent, that being twice the window and not longer than it; one priced 61 days ago carries 10 percent.
